title: Senior VP, AML Operations_ Group Retail
VP of Quality
description:
**About Lumilens**

At Lumilens we are building the critical photonics infrastructure that powers tomorrow’s AI supercomputing. From chip-to-chip optical interconnects to scalable photonic engines, Lumilens is unlocking a new era of computing - faster, cooler, and massively more efficient.

We’re a well-funded startup backed by Mayfield and led by veterans who’ve built and scaled some of the most transformative technologies in the industry. At Lumilens, we’re developing high-speed photonics products purpose-built to power the future of AI infrastructure and high-performance computing.

This isn’t incremental innovation, it’s a ground-floor opportunity to rethink the optical layer from the silicon up. You’ll work alongside a team of world-class engineers solving some of the hardest challenges in scaling optical systems. Every line of code, every design decision, every breakthrough you help deliver will shape the infrastructure of tomorrow.

If you're looking for mission, momentum, and the chance to make an outsized impact, jump on the rocket ship. We’re just getting started.

**About the role**

We are looking for a VP of Quality to build and lead Lumilens' global quality and reliability organization as we scale our optical interconnect products, including 800G/1.6T pluggable transceivers, near-package optics, and co-packaged optics, from qualification to high-volume production for hyperscale data center customers. You will own quality end to end, from design and suppliers through manufacturing, customer qualification, and field performance, and you will be the company's quality voice with our most demanding customers. This is a senior leadership role that partners closely with Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, and Sales, and reports to executive leadership.

**Responsibilities**

* Define the quality and reliability strategy for Lumilens, and grow and lead a high-performing team spanning quality engineering, reliability engineering, supplier quality, customer quality, and quality management systems.
* Establish and scale a Quality Management System (QMS) certified to ISO 9001, including document control, change management, internal and external audits, and quarterly business reviews for our own sites and our contract manufacturing and OSAT partners.
* Own product reliability and qualification for lasers, photonic integrated circuits (PICs), and optical modules, including test strategy aligned with Telcordia GR-468, JEDEC, and customer-specific requirements (e.g., HTOL, damp heat, temperature cycling, accelerated aging, storage), reliability modeling (FIT rates, wear-out, MTTF), and ongoing reliability testing (ORT).
* Serve as the primary quality interface for hyperscaler and OEM customers. Lead customer qualifications, audits, and quality agreements, and own quality scorecards, RMAs, and 8D corrective action responses within committed timelines.
* Build a supplier quality program for critical components, including lasers, PICs, DSPs, optics, substrates, fiber array units, etc. Partner with contract manufacturers and OSATs to meet our corporate quality standards.
* Embed quality into our new product introduction (NPI) process: Partner with Engineering on DFMEA/PFMEA, design reviews, control plans, and phase-gate exit criteria to ensure products are designed for reliability and manufacturability.
* Drive manufacturing quality through the production ramp: set and achieve DPPM, yield, and outgoing quality targets, and deploy SPC, process capability (Cpk), test coverage, and containment practices.
* Build failure analysis (FA) capabilities for optical, electrical, and materials analysis, in-house and with external labs, to drive fast and rigorous root-cause analysis.
* Implement quality data systems and end-to-end traceability (serial- and lot-level, integrated with MES and test data) to provide early warning of yield, reliability, and field issues.
* Monitor field performance of deployed products in customer data centers, and lead escalations, containment, and corrective actions when issues arise.
* Ensure compliance with relevant standards and regulations, including ESD control (ANSI/ESD S20.20), cleanroom and contamination control, laser safety (IEC 60825-1), and environmental requirements (RoHS, REACH, conflict minerals).
* Report quality KPIs and cost of quality to the executive team and Board, and build a culture of continuous improvement, data-driven decision making, and ownership of quality across the company.
* Lead quality across multiple sites and regions, including manufacturing operations and partners in Asia.

**Qualifications**

* 15+ years of experience in quality and reliability for optical, photonics, or semiconductor hardware, including at least 5 years leading quality organizations at Director or VP level.
* Proven track record of taking products from NPI to high-volume production, ideally for transceiver, hyperscale data center or major networking OEM customers.
* Deep expertise in optoelectronic reliability and qualification and in failure mechanisms of lasers, PICs, and optical packaging.
* Experience building or scaling an ISO 9001 QMS, and leading customer and third-party audits.
* Strong supplier quality experience with contract manufacturers and OSATs, particularly in Asia.
* Strong command of statistical and quality methods. Six Sigma Black Belt or ASQ CQE/CRE certification is a plus.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work under pressure in customer escalations and to influence across Engineering, Operations, and leadership.
* Bachelor's degree in Quality Management, Supply Chain, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Optics, Materials Science, or a related field. Master's or PhD preferred.
* A builder's mindset suited to a fast-scaling startup, and willingness to travel internationally to sites, suppliers, and customers.

title: Director, Validation
description:
**Location** Singapore, Singapore, Singapore **Job ID** R-264566 **Date posted** 18/11/2026

  

**Job Title: Director, Validation**

**Career Level: F**

**About Singapore ADC Site:**

Be part of history in the making. AstraZeneca is building its first biologics manufacturing campus in Singapore — a groundbreaking USD 1.5 billion investment that will serve as a global hub for innovation and excellence.

This innovative facility will deliver end-to-end Antibody-Drug Conjugate (ADC) capabilities with different manufacturing units/buildings in one campus:

* Small molecule- chemical API production
* Large molecule- monoclonal antibody manufacturing
* Conjugation
* Fill-and-finish operations, including sterile filling and lyophilization
* Final secondary packaging

The campus will be equipped with innovative digital and automation infrastructure, enabling autonomous manufacturing powered by artificial intelligence. In addition, it will be designed for carbon neutrality, embedding sustainability into every aspect of operations and setting a new benchmark for environmentally responsible biologic's manufacturing.

In Manufacturing, Science and Technology Team, we are looking for passionate individuals with relevant experience who thrive in dynamic environments and bring a “make-it-happen” attitude. Joining us means contributing to a project that will not only transform AstraZeneca’s global supply chain but also advance life-changing medicines for patients everywhere.

If you’re ready to shape the future of biologics and be part of a once-in-a-generation project, we want you on our team.

**Introduction to role:**

Are you ready to lead site-wide validation that enables complex biologics and antibody-drug conjugates to reach patients safely and at speed? Do you want to shape a risk-based validation program that keeps a new, high-impact facility inspection-ready and continuously improving?

As Director of Validation for our Singapore ADC Manufacturing facility, you will set the strategic direction for qualification and validation across equipment, facilities, utilities, IT systems and processes. Your leadership will ensure alignment with AstraZeneca standards, current regulatory expectations and industry standard process, building and sustaining a robust state of control across this high-potency, aseptic environment. You will lead lifecycle validation, drive cleaning validation and sterility assurance programs, and own validation governance at the site. Partnering closely with Quality, Regulatory, Manufacturing and Global Technical collaborators, you will enable reliable, efficient supply while advancing modern validation methodologies and digital ways of working.

**Accountabilities:**

* Validation Strategy and Governance: Define and maintain the Site Validation Master Plan and project VMPs, setting risk-based strategies, requalification requirements and lifecycle approaches that keep the facility fully compliant and inspection-ready.
* Lifecycle Qualification and State of Control: Lead the end-to-end qualification and validation of equipment, utilities, HVAC and computerised systems, ensuring cGMP compliance, data integrity and sustained control over time.
* Cleaning and Sterility Assurance Oversight: Own the site’s cleaning validation and sterility assurance programs, including thermal sterilisation, SIP, depyrogenation and VHP decontamination, to protect product quality and patient safety.
* Team Leadership and Capability Building: Manage, mentor and coach a multidisciplinary team, building technical excellence, accountability and continuous improvement in validation practices.
* Documentation and Compliance Excellence: Ensure timely, high-quality risk assessments, protocols, reports and SOPs; drive closure of preventive and corrective actions and uphold data-driven, right-first-time documentation.
* Project and Change Leadership: Lead validation projects and change control for equipment and systems to meet safety, quality, regulatory and operational requirements, from specification and design through installation and qualification.
* Regulatory Engagement and Inspection Readiness: Defend commissioning, design and qualification of GMP equipment during inspections; participate in and support audits.
* Data-Driven Decisions and Investigations: Perform and guide analysis, lead or support investigations, and enable sound decisions using appropriate methodologies to resolve issues and prevent recurrence.
* Budget Ownership and Resource Prioritization: Establish and manage the validation budget, aligning resources to priorities and delivering value and efficiency.
* Regulatory Intelligence and Best Practice: Monitor evolving regulatory expectations and industry standards, proactively adapting site approaches to remain at the forefront of validation guidelines.

**Essential Skills/Experience:**

* University degree or equivalent experience in Chemical Engineering, Biochemical Engineering, Chemistry, Mechanical Engineering or a related field.
* Minimum of 7–10 years of experience in biopharma MSAT, process engineering or validation, with direct technical leadership at commercial scale.
* Experience with the risk-based verification approach and ASTM E2500.
* Direct experience of, or oversight in, performing equipment, utilities, HVAC and/or computerised system qualification studies in cGMP aseptic biologics manufacturing and high-potency API.
* Direct experience of, or oversight in, validation studies of thermal sterilisation processes, including autoclave validation, steam-in-place (SIP) validation, and validation of depyrogenation and decontamination (VHP) processes.

**Desirable Skills/Experience:**

* Project management skills.
* ADC or high-potency manufacturing experience, including occupational exposure controls and containment requirements.

When we put unexpected teams in the same room, we unleash bold thinking with the power to inspire life-changing medicines. In-person working gives us the platform we need to connect, work at pace and challenge perceptions. That's why we work, on average, a minimum of three days per week from the office. But that doesn't mean we're not flexible. We balance the expectation of being in the office while respecting individual flexibility. Join us in our unique and ambitious world.

**Why AstraZeneca:**

Here you will feel the energy of a company scaling modern manufacturing to deliver more medicines, faster and more affordably, without compromising safety or quality. You will collaborate in diverse, co-located teams that combine innovative science, Lean thinking and fast-evolving digital technologies to move from molecule to medicine with precision. We value kindness alongside ambition, and we invest deeply in people, so they can lead, learn and stretch across a truly global network. Your contribution will help turn complex pipelines into reliable supply, advance sustainable practices, and set new benchmarks for validation excellence that directly benefit patients and society.

**Call to Action:**

Bring your expertise to Singapore and help build a benchmark validation program for ADC manufacturing—submit your application and shape what comes next.

19-Nov-2026

**Closing Date**

03-Dec-2026

AstraZeneca embraces diversity and equality of opportunity. We are committed to building an inclusive and diverse team representing all backgrounds, with as wide a range of perspectives as possible, and harnessing industry-leading skills. title: Senior Manager, Digital Transformation (Corporate Services)
description:
At Singapore Children’s Society, we are committed to improving the well-being of children, youth and families through services that are responsive, evidence-informed and focused on lasting impact. Our digital transformation strengthens this mission by reducing administrative burden, connecting systems and information, and enabling staff to spend more time on people and outcomes.
  
  
The Digital Transformation function leads organisation-wide process redesign and the responsible adoption of digital, data and automation solutions. If you can bring services and corporate functions units, technology partners/vendors and leaders together to turn operational challenges into simpler, secure and sustainable ways of working, we invite you to join us.
  
  
Work Objectives
  
  
As Senior Manager, Digital Transformation, you will lead the Society’s digital transformation portfolio, translating organisational priorities into a coherent roadmap of process redesign, workflow digitisation, system integration, data use and capability building. You will partner with centres and departments to clarify outcomes, redesign work before automating it, determine suitable build-or-buy approaches, and lead initiatives from discovery through implementation, adoption and benefits realisation.
  
  
Reporting to the Director, Corporate Services, you will establish practical delivery and governance disciplines across the portfolio while working closely with business owners, IT, data protection, cybersecurity, Finance, HR and external partners. You will strengthen internal capability in low-code and no-code enabled digital workflow solutions, automation and digital change, track measurable benefits such as time saved, adoption and user satisfaction, and ensure that solutions remain user-centred, secure, compliant, integrated and maintainable.
  
  
Key Responsibilities
  
  
1. Digital Transformation Strategy and Portfolio Leadership
  
  
Develop, maintain and execute a prioritised, multi-year digital transformation roadmap aligned with the Society’s mission, organisational transformation plans and digital strategy.
  
  
Translate strategic priorities and operational pain points into a governed portfolio of process, data, automation and technology initiatives with clear outcomes, owners, dependencies, resources and delivery sequence.
  
  
Advise leaders on solution options and build-or-buy decisions, balancing user needs, value, integration, security, compliance, scalability, cost and long-term supportability.
  
  
Provide decision-ready progress, risk, benefit and resource reporting to governance bodies and senior management, and escalate issues requiring intervention or reprioritisation.
  
  
2. Business Process Redesign and Solution Delivery
  
  
Lead end-to-end discovery and redesign of cross-functional workflows using user research, process mapping, systems thinking and value analysis before digitisation or automation.
  
  
Partner with business owners to define future-state processes, business requirements, service standards, controls and measurable success indicators.
  
  
Lead digital initiatives from business case and requirements through procurement or configuration, testing, implementation, integration, transition and post-implementation review.
  
  
Build or oversee fit-for-purpose internal workflow solutions using low-code, no-code, automation and analytics platforms where appropriate, while engaging specialised vendors for complex or external-facing systems.
  
  
3. Adoption, Change and Capability Enablement
  
  
Design and implement change and adoption plans that build leadership sponsorship, staff ownership, digital confidence and sustained use of new ways of working.
  
  
Facilitate workshops, design sessions, pilots and retrospectives that help teams surface constraints, test solutions and improve implementation.
  
  
Develop practical playbooks, templates and standards for process redesign, product ownership, project delivery, benefits tracking and continuous improvement.
  
  
Grow a network of digital champions and provide coaching, training and hands-on support to strengthen digital, data, AI and automation capabilities across the organisation.
  
  
4. Governance, Risk and Sustainable Operations
  
  
Embed privacy, cybersecurity, records management, accessibility, safeguarding and relevant regulatory requirements into solution design and delivery in partnership with control functions.
  
  
Establish proportionate governance for intake, prioritisation, architecture, data, change control, testing, release, vendor management and operational handover.
  
  
Ensure digital solutions have clear ownership, documentation, support arrangements, service expectations, business continuity considerations and lifecycle plans.
  
  
Maintain portfolio records, decisions, risks, dependencies, budgets and benefits evidence using consistent repositories and version control.
  
  
5. Data, Insights and Benefits Realisation
  
  
Define baselines, targets and SMART measures for each initiative, including administrative time saved, process quality, staff adoption, user experience, cost avoidance and service outcomes where relevant.
  
  
Use dashboards, qualitative feedback and operational data to monitor delivery, adoption and impact, and recommend corrective action or scaling decisions.
  
  
Promote reliable data capture, appropriate integration and one-source-of-truth practices that improve reporting and decision-making.
  
  
Capture and share lessons across initiatives so that successful approaches can be standardised, reused and scaled.
  
  
6. Team Leadership and Stakeholder Partnership
  
  
Lead, coach and supervise assigned team members or project resources, setting clear expectations and assuring the quality and timeliness of outputs.
  
  
Build trusted partnerships with centre and department leaders, frontline users, corporate functions, vendors, funders and sector partners.
  
  
Clarify business ownership and decision rights, ensuring that business units own outcomes and processes while technology teams enable architecture, security, integration and sustainable implementation.
  
  
Represent the Digital Transformation function in internal and external engagements, and deputise for the Director, Corporate Services when specifically designated and within delegated authority.
  
  
Job Requirements
  
  
Qualifications
  
  
Bachelor’s degree in information systems, business, engineering, organisational development, public administration, service design or a related discipline.
  
  
Relevant qualifications or certifications in digital transformation, business process improvement, change management, product or project management, data analytics, low-code platforms (Zoho Creator, Jodoo etc) or agile delivery are advantageous.
  
  
Experience
  
  
At least eight to ten years of relevant experience, including substantial responsibility for digital transformation, business process redesign, technology-enabled change or enterprise improvement initiatives.
  
  
Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives from discovery and business case (HRMS/ through implementation, adoption and benefits realisation.
  
  
Hands-on experience improving workflows through low-code or no-code platforms, automation, analytics, enterprise applications or integrated digital services.
  
  
Experience working with senior leaders, frontline users, corporate functions, vendors and multidisciplinary delivery teams.
  
  
Experience establishing delivery governance, managing budgets and suppliers, and tracking risks, dependencies, adoption and measurable benefits.
  
  
Experience in the social service, public service, healthcare, education or other mission-driven sector is an advantage.
  
  
Skills
  
  
Strong business process analysis and redesign capability, including process mapping, user-centred design, requirements definition and future-state operating design.
  
  
Strong programme, project or product leadership, with disciplined prioritisation, planning, delivery, risk management, quality assurance and follow-through.
  
  
Working knowledge of enterprise systems, integration, data governance, cybersecurity, privacy and technology lifecycle considerations.
  
  
Competence with low-code or no-code automation and analytics platforms such as Microsoft Power Platform, Power BI or equivalent tools.
  
  
Strong change leadership, facilitation and stakeholder-engagement skills, including the ability to build alignment across differing priorities and levels of digital confidence.
  
  
Excellent analytical, communication and writing skills, with the ability to translate operational complexity and technical choices into clear recommendations for senior audiences.
  
  
Commercial and vendor-management acumen, including procurement support, scope and service review, delivery assurance and contract performance monitoring.
  
  
Attributes
  
  
Purpose-driven and committed to improving outcomes for children, youth and families through practical, responsible digital transformation.
  
  
User-centred, curious and willing to understand work at the frontline before proposing solutions.
  
  
Pragmatic and outcomes-focused, with the discipline to simplify processes before automating them and to measure whether change has delivered value.
  
  
Collaborative and influential, able to build trust, challenge constructively and create shared ownership across organisational boundaries.
  
  
Comfortable with complexity, ambiguity and competing priorities, while maintaining sound judgement, structure and momentum.
  
  
Accountable and attentive to quality, security, privacy, confidentiality, sustainability and follow-through.
  
  
Learning-oriented and adaptable, with the confidence to test, iterate, stop low-value work and scale what works.
  
  
About Singapore Children’s Society
  
  
Singapore Children’s Society protects and nurtures children and youth of all races and religions. In 2025, the Society reached out to 22,333 children, youth and families in need. Established in 1952, its services have evolved to meet the changing needs of children.
  
  
Today, Children’s Society operates more than 10 service centres islandwide, offering services in the four categories of: Vulnerable Children and Youth, Children and Youth Services, Family Services, and Research and Advocacy.
  
  
Our Patron-in-Chief is President Tharman Shanmugaratnam.
  
  
Our
  
  
Mission
  
  
We champion the wellbeing of children and youth by shifting mindsets and creating lasting change
  
  
Our
  
  
Vision
  
  
A future where every child and youth enjoys a safe and happy childhood and flourishes in strong families and caring communities
  
  
Our
  
  
Core Values
  
  
Compassion and Caring, Commitment, Professionalism, Integrity, and Openness to Change
  
  
For more information, please you can also watch our latest corporate video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UW\_xE\_3y-nY

title: Senior Director - Technical and Self-Delivery Services
description:
**Job Title**

Senior Director - Technical and Self-Delivery Services

**Job Description Summary**

Lead the internal Technical and Self-Delivery Services platform (M&E, HVAC/ACMV, lifts and escalators, rope access, cleaning and projects) that serves the Integrated Facilities Management (IFM) business. Deliver safe, compliant, high-quality services at a competitive cost, with the primary focus on cost control, productivity, process optimisation and right-first-time quality.

**Job Description**

**About the Job:**

* **Cost and finance:** Own the S$50 million cost base across every service line, leading budgeting, rolling forecasts and monthly variance reviews. Deliver sustainable savings in labour, subcontractor, materials and project spend without degrading quality, deferring essential maintenance or increasing risk.
* **Productivity:** Build a data-led operating model covering workforce planning, rostering, scheduling and resource deployment. Raise productive utilisation and first-time-fix rates while reducing overtime, repeat visits and non-productive time across mobile and site-based teams.
* **Process optimisation:** Simplify and standardise end-to-end workflows from work-order intake to completion and reporting. Apply Lean methods, digital field tools, mechanisation and cleaning robotics, and own a multi-year improvement roadmap with verified annualised savings.
* **Quality and technical authority:** Act as senior custodian of quality and technical governance, setting standards (using locally / globally recognised standards as a minimum), inspection regimes and competency requirements. Govern maintenance against statutory and OEM requirements, and lead root-cause reviews of repeat defects, callbacks and complaints.
* **Service lines:** Provide governance and performance leadership for each specialist service line, supported by discipline leads and SMEs. Hold each line accountable for reliability, statutory compliance, productivity, quality and safe delivery.
* **IFM partnership:** Build strong relationships with IFM leadership and account teams, agreeing service catalogues, internal SLAs, cost-to-serve assumptions and escalation routes. Support bids, solution design and new contract mobilisations to show the value of self-delivery.
* **People:** Lead and develop a workforce of approximately 300 employees, from supervisors and engineers to technicians and operatives. Own organisation design, succession, recruitment and retention, and build a culture of accountability, visible leadership and continuous improvement.
* **Safety and compliance:** Maintain uncompromising safety and compliance standards across high-risk work, including permit-to-work, working at height, rope access, lift and escalator safety. Ensure sound risk assessments, contractor governance, incident investigation and consistent sharing of lessons learned.

**About You:**

* Degree or professional qualification in Mechanical, Electrical or Building Services Engineering (or related).
* At least 15 years’ experience in engineering services, facilities management or building services, including leading 200+ staff and a significant budget.
* Strong mechanical, electrical and HVAC/ACMV background, with credibility as a senior technical authority.
* Proven record in cost optimisation, productivity, process standardisation and operational excellence.
* Experience supporting IFM contracts, mobilisations and bids; exposure to lifts, rope access and cleaning is desirable. Understanding (including application) of global standards (i.e. SFG20, BICS, EN13015, ISO 22846, etc).
* Strong financial, commercial, analytical and stakeholder-management skills with the ability to translate operational data into actionable business insights and measurable performance improvements
* Desirable: Chartered/Professional Engineer; asset, facilities or project management; Lean Six Sigma.

title: Senior Director, HR
description:
A world empowered by autonomy. We build robotic vehicles to improve logistics safety, forge a greener Earth, and enhance human lives.
  
  
We are a closely-knit team aspiring to change the world through disruptive technology. We are innovators. We are tinkerers. We are problem-solvers. And we have a fair amount of magic dust up our sleeves. We have a plan for fleet-level deployment of autonomous vehicles, and we are looking for the best-of-the-best to join us in making this a reality.
  
  
About Venti Technologies
  
  
Based in the U.S. and Asia, Venti Technologies is the leader in safe-speed autonomous logistics systems, developing the future of goods transportation. Using rigorous mathematics, deep learning, and theoretically-grounded algorithms, Venti has a proprietary collection of autonomy technologies including a suite of powerful logistics algorithms. Venti’s proven value proposition of saving costs, increasing vehicle utilization, and improving safety is recognized by customers and driving growth. Launched in 2018, Venti brings together an unsurpassed team internationally. The company has autonomous systems deployed in Asia for industrial and logistics sites and a growing pipeline. Venti has offices in Cambridge (Massachusetts, USA), Suzhou (China), and Singapore – our Asian headquarters.
  
  
The Opportunity
  
  
We are looking for an experienced, commercially minded HR leader to lead our global people function as the business continues to grow.
  
  
This is a broad, hands-on leadership role, partnering with the CEO and leadership team to develop the organisation, attract and retain exceptional talent, strengthen our culture and build the people practices and infrastructure needed to support the company's next stage of growth. You will lead a team of 3 (including office management). The company is expanding into the US with a number of deployments, and the successful candidate will be comfortable working globally.
  
  
Key Responsibilities
  
  
**People Strategy:**  
Continue to evolve and execute our HR strategy aligned with business priorities and growth ambitions.
  
  
**Talent & Leadership:**  
Lead talent acquisition, development, performance management, succession planning and leadership effectiveness.
  
  
**Organisation & Culture:**  
Shape organisational design, strengthen company culture and build an inclusive, high-performance environment.
  
  
**HR Operations:**  
Establish scalable HR processes, policies, compensation and benefits programmes, and employee lifecycle practices.
  
  
**Employee Relations & Compliance:**  
Provide effective guidance on employee matters and ensure compliance with relevant employment laws and regulations.
  
  
**Leadership Partnership:**  
Act as a trusted advisor to the CEO, leadership team and managers on organisational and people-related priorities.
  
  
Experience & Attributes
  
  
15+ years of broad HR experience, ideally in a growing technology, engineering or other technically complex business.
  
  
Proven experience building and scaling HR capabilities in a dynamic, international environment.
  
  
Experience in consulting is preferred, as is strong international work experience.
  
  
Strong track record across talent acquisition, organisational development, leadership development and performance management, both personally and through team development
  
  
Commercially minded, analytical and comfortable translating business needs into practical people solutions.
  
  
Equally comfortable setting strategy and rolling up your sleeves to deliver.
  
  
Strong interpersonal, communication and influencing skills, with the ability to build credibility across different cultures and levels of the organisation.
  
  
Culturally adaptable, able to build trust in many different contexts.
  
  
High integrity, sound judgement and a collaborative, pragmatic approach.
  
  
Salary is commensurate with experience. We also offer world-class benefits, fantastic culture, flexible working arrangements, and a great international working environment. Come and join us!
  
  
Venti is the global leader in the $175 billion AV logistics hubs market. Founded in 2018 with technology developed in MIT professor Rus' lab, we develop, sell, and deploy software systems for driverless vehicles in ports, factories, warehouses, and communities.
  
  
**Venti gives customers a clear value proposition:** Removing drivers saves multiple driver-shift costs, increases vehicle utilization by 15%+, and significantly improves safety. This translates to savings per vehicle-year of $150,000 - $220,000 in US and $60,000 - $90,000 in Asia.
  
  
Our powerful strategic partners are pathways for explosive growth.
  
  
AV Container Movers for ports with PSA, the most respected port operator in the world with 60 ports under management AV Tug Trailer systems with SAIC Anji Logistics, the largest automotive logistics company in the world. Small last-mile vehicles with Seedland, a large real estate developer and operator
  
  
The company benchmarked #1 in the world in Perception tech - the core of autonomy - in 2020.
  
  
Our powerful autonomy system has powered 12 different vehicle types. We beat the competition in cost and quality: new vehicle deployment within a week, area mapping in a morning, factor of five cost reduction for sensors and hardware.
  
  
Come ride with us into the future.

title: Director, Securities Audit Lead, Internal Audit Department - SMBC

title: PROJECT DIRECTOR
description:
To provide overall leadership and strategic direction for the company's façade projects, ensuring successful project delivery, profitability, operational efficiency, and client satisfaction.
  
  
The Project Director is responsible for overseeing all project operations, managing senior project teams, controlling project financial performance, resolving major contractual and operational issues, and ensuring the company's project objectives and business targets are achieved.
  
  
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  
  
A. Overall Project & Operations Management
  
  
Oversee all façade projects from contract award to final completion and handover.
  
  
Establish project execution strategies, priorities, and overall operational plans.
  
  
Ensure projects are delivered on schedule, within budget, and according to contractual requirements.
  
  
Monitor overall project performance and resolve major project issues and risks.
  
  
Allocate manpower, resources, and equipment effectively across projects.
  
  
Report project performance and operational matters to senior management.
  
  
B. Commercial & Financial Management
  
  
Take overall responsibility for project profitability, budgets, cost control, and cash flow.
  
  
Review project financial performance and ensure targeted gross profit margins are achieved.
  
  
Oversee progress claims, payment collection, VO submissions, and contractual claims.
  
  
Ensure Senior Project Managers actively pursue outstanding VO approvals, certifications, and payments.
  
  
Lead major commercial negotiations with clients and main contractors.
  
  
Monitor project cost overruns and implement appropriate cost-control measures.
  
  
C. Contract & Risk Management
  
  
Oversee contractual obligations and ensure the company's commercial interests are protected.
  
  
Review major contractual issues, variations, extensions of time (EOT), and claims.
  
  
Identify potential project risks and implement mitigation strategies.
  
  
Resolve major disputes and contractual disagreements with clients and main contractors.
  
  
D. Technical & Project Delivery
  
  
Provide strategic direction on façade design, engineering, procurement, fabrication, and installation.
  
  
Oversee technical coordination and ensure compliance with project specifications and statutory requirements.
  
  
Ensure quality standards, testing requirements, and safety regulations are maintained.
  
  
Drive improvements in project execution, productivity, and operational efficiency.
  
  
E. Client & Business Relationship Management
  
  
Maintain strong relationships with key clients, consultants, developers, and main contractors.
  
  
Lead high-level project and commercial meetings.
  
  
Resolve major client complaints and project escalations.
  
  
Support business development activities, tender reviews, and new project opportunities.
  
  
F. Leadership & Team Development
  
  
Lead, mentor, and manage Senior Project Managers and Project Management Teams.
  
  
Establish clear project objectives, responsibilities, and performance targets.
  
  
Monitor team performance and ensure accountability across all projects.
  
  
Develop future project leaders and strengthen the company's project management capabilities.
  
  
Promote teamwork, professionalism, quality, and safety culture.
  
  
3. QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE
  
  
Degree in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, Building Construction, or a related discipline.
  
  
Minimum 15–20 years of relevant facade industry experience.
  
  
Proven experience in managing large-scale and multiple façade projects.
  
  
Strong track record in project financial management, commercial negotiations, contract administration, and VO recovery.
  
  
Extensive knowledge of curtain walls, aluminium windows, glazing, cladding, and façade systems.
  
  
Preferably able to communicate in mandarin to facilitate effective communication and coordination with Chinese speaking clients, consultant, supplier and sub contractors
  
  
Preferably experienced in managing project operations within a façade specialist contractor.
  
  
A specialist façade construction company providing comprehensive building façade solutions, including curtain wall systems, glass and aluminum installations, and external cladding works.

title: AVP, Audit Manager, Group Governance and Corporate Functions Audit
description:
**WHO WE ARE:**
===============

As Singapore’s longest established bank, we have been dedicated to enabling individuals and businesses to achieve their aspirations since 1932. How? By taking the time to truly understand people. From there, we provide support, services, solutions, and career paths that meet their individual needs and desires.

Today, we’re on a journey of transformation. Leveraging technology and creativity to become a future-ready learning organisation. But for all that change, our strategic ambition is consistently clear and bold, which is to be Asia’s leading financial services partner for a sustainable future.

We invite you to build the bank of the future. Innovate the way we deliver financial services. Work in friendly, supportive teams. Build lasting value in your community. Help people grow their assets, business, and investments. Take your learning as far as you can. Or simply enjoy a vibrant, future-ready career.

Your Opportunity Starts Here.

**Why Join**
============

Join OCBC to be part of a dynamic and forward-thinking organisation that values innovation and collaboration. In Group Audit, you’ll enjoy a unique perspective across the Bank, gaining insights into diverse functions while driving impactful change. It’s an opportunity to strengthen governance, assess risks, and contribute to the Bank’s resilience and OneGroup vision. With continuous learning opportunities, it’s a rewarding role for those passionate about making a difference.

**How You Succeed**
===================

To succeed in Group Audit at OCBC, one must combine critical thinking with a keen eye for detail. Build strong stakeholder relationships, ask the right questions, and challenge assumptions. Leverage data analytics for sharper insights and stay updated on emerging risks and trends. Managing multiple priorities, adapting to complex situations, and maintaining independence are key. Resilience and effective communication will help navigate challenges and deliver impactful, high-quality audit outcomes.

**What You Do**
===============

**Audit Management**

* Support the Group Portfolio Leads and/or Senior Audit Managers in Group-wide audit engagements, including planning, scoping, risk assessments and communication. Ensure that risks and control deficiencies related to the governance framework, risk management, regulatory compliance processes and internal control systems of the OCBC Banking Group have been identified, appropriately assessed, and reported.
* Conduct Group-wide audits/reviews on:
* Financial Crime Compliance (including fraud risk);
* Operational Risk Management (including Business Continuity Management, Self-assessment and Third-party Risk Management, etc);
* Legal and Regulatory Compliance and key activities of the corporate functions (including Human Resources, Brand and Communications, Corporate Secretariat, etc); and
* Property and Procurement Services.
Participate in the provision of advisory services and ad-hoc reviews (e.g. special reviews at the request of senior management or regulators) with the objective of adding value and improving the governance, risk management, and control processes of the OCBC Banking Group, without Group Audit assuming management responsibility.  

**Stakeholder Management**

* Work as business partners with stakeholders and senior leadership across the Group, to communicate audit findings and agree on appropriate risk mitigation and remediation actions.
* Foster strong and enduring relationships with the business and act as a trusted advisor on risk and controls related to financial crime compliance, operational risk management as well as the key activities of the corporate functions.
* Support the Group Functional Head and/or Group Portfolio Lead in identifying any need for changes to the audit plan to address any emerging risks and concerns, regulatory developments or shifts in the OCBC Banking Group’s corporate strategy.
Provide regular updates to the Group Functional Head and/or Group Portfolio Lead and senior management on audit progress, key risks and action plans.  

**Team Management**

* Support the execution of guest auditor programs.
* Complete working papers for audits/reviews through documenting the work conducted, describing the work performed and the evidence that supports the observations and conclusions, as well as reviewing the work performed by other team members.
Promote innovation by encouraging the use of advanced data analytics, automation, and AI/ML tools to enhance audit efficiency and effectiveness.  

**Internal Audit Practice Management**

* Apply audit methodology, standards, and practices that are relevant to the OCBC Banking Group, taking into consideration leading practices in internal auditing.

* Support the implementation of a quality assurance and improvement program to assess Group Audit’s conformance with the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA) International Standards for the Professional Practice of Internal Auditing and establish measures to address any gaps and enhance internal audit practices.

Where necessary, assist the Group Portfolio Lead in engaging external service provider for co-sourcing of internal audit activities, ensuring adequate oversight of the external service provider.  

  

**Who You Work With**
=====================

Group Audit is all about oversight. Gaining experience of the bank in its entirety. Gathering insight. Building Risk and Controls expertise. Advising leadership. You might join us in Global Markets, Risk and Finance Audit, Credit Risk Audit, Investigation, Professional Practices and Governance or Audit Analytics. But wherever you are, your work with clients from around the world drives innovation and makes audit an artform.

**Who You Are**
===============

* Holds a bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (e.g. Business, Accountancy, etc.)
* Professional certifications such as CPA, CA, CIA and/or ACAMS are highly preferred
* Minimum of 5 years of experience in auditing or other risk control functions
* Strong understanding of risks and controls pertaining to Banking, with a focus on financial crime compliance (including fraud risk), regulatory compliance, operational risk management and corporate functions
* Good written, verbal communication and presentation skills, with the ability to translate technical issues into relevant business context for senior management
* Ability to work effectively as a team member, with the requisite analytical skills to perform detailed/technical work without losing sight of the ‘big picture’ issues
* High level of integrity, drive, and ability to work under pressure
* Data analytics skills (e.g. knowledge of Python, Power BI or other data analytics tool) are preferred
* undefined

**What we offer:**
==================

Competitive base salary. A suite of holistic, flexible benefits to suit every lifestyle. Community initiatives. Industry-leading learning and professional development opportunities. Your wellbeing, growth and aspirations are every bit as cared for as the needs of our customers.

title: Analyst, Internal Control (Job ID:10080744)
description:
MUFG is seeking a dedicated Internal Control Professional to join their Planning Department, Internal Control and Administration team for GCIB in Singapore. This role offers you the opportunity to play a pivotal part in ensuring robust governance and effective control activities across the division. You will be at the heart of maintaining high standards of compliance, supporting business continuity, and safeguarding information security within one of the world’s leading financial institutions. MUFG values your commitment to accuracy, your collaborative spirit, and your ability to connect with stakeholders across departments. The organisation is renowned for its supportive leadership, inclusive culture, and ongoing training opportunities that empower you to grow professionally while contributing meaningfully to the team’s success.
  
  
Join a globally respected financial institution where your attention to detail and commitment to quality will directly impact divisional governance and operational excellence.
  
  
Work closely with diverse teams and stakeholders, fostering strong inter-personal connections and sharing knowledge to ensure seamless implementation of internal controls.
  
  
Benefit from MUFG’s commitment to professional development, working opportunities, and a supportive team environment that values collaboration and knowledge sharing.
  
  
**What you'll do:**  
As an Internal Control professional at MUFG in Singapore, you will take on a multifaceted role spanning internal controls, governance, operational resilience and management support. Working closely with various departments, you will help ensure that GCIB maintains effective controls, appropriate governance standards and accurate control-related records.
  
  
Your responsibilities will include coordinating GCIB self-inspections, managing SOX reporting processes, tracking remediation actions and following up on findings through to closure. You will also coordinate business continuity management activities, including disaster recovery exercises, and maintain critical records such as call trees and next-of-kin information.
  
  
In addition to overseeing and driving greater consistency in SOPs and governance documentation on SharePoint, you will support non-system information security controls to help ensure appropriate standards for information handling are maintained. You will also monitor incidents and support timely escalation and reporting where required.
  
  
Your responsibilities will extend to vault governance, including record reconciliation and periodic access reviews, as well as the maintenance of authorities-related documentation, including Letters of Delegation of Authority, Deeds of Substitution and authorised signature lists.
  
  
You will also provide ad-hoc administrative and management support to help ensure the smooth running of the department. Success in this role requires strong attention to detail, sound control awareness and the ability to work effectively across multiple stakeholders, while remaining flexible and adaptable to changing business priorities.
  
  

* Perform and coordinate GCIB self-inspection processes, SOX reporting and spreadsheet controls, including the management of findings, supporting evidence, remediation tracking and follow-up actions.
* Oversee and drive greater consistency in standard operating procedures (SOPs), RACI matrices and internal guidelines, and maintain related governance documentation on GCIB SharePoint.
* Perform and coordinate business continuity management activities, including business impact analysis, call tree and next-of-kin record maintenance, disaster recovery exercises and other related activities.
* Serve as PIC for non-system information security controls, including data-handling requirements and information security exceptions, in accordance with Bank policies.
* Serve as PIC for incident monitoring and reporting, ensuring timely escalation, communication and accurate documentation of events affecting divisional operations.
* Manage GCIB Vault governance, including regular record reconciliation, access reviews and implementation of relevant controls to safeguard sensitive materials.
* Serve as PIC for authorities-related governance, including Letters of Authority, Deeds of Substitution and Powers of Attorney, and maintain the division’s authorised signature list.
* Provide administrative and management support as assigned by the Head of Department or Management, including ad-hoc responsibilities that contribute to the effective operation of the team.
* Collaborate with relevant departments and stakeholders to support the timely and accurate implementation of internal requirements, Head Office procedures and Bank policies.
* Maintain robust control-related records and procedures and support effective governance across GCIB functions.

**What you bring:**  
To excel as an Internal Control professional at MUFG in Singapore, you bring proven experience from roles involving internal control or audit functions, ideally within financial services. Your academic background equips you with essential theoretical understanding while your practical experience ensures you can navigate complex regulatory environments confidently. You possess exceptional attention to detail which allows you not only to spot inconsistencies but also deliver high-quality results every time. Managing competing priorities under tight deadlines is second nature; you remain calm yet responsive even when demands escalate. Communication is one of your strengths—you engage openly with colleagues at all levels fostering trustful relationships that drive collective achievement. Professionalism defines how you handle sensitive matters; integrity guides every decision you make. Your proactive attitude means you anticipate needs before they arise while collaborating seamlessly within teams regardless of pace or change. Technical proficiency across Microsoft tools supports your daily workflow; familiarity with business continuity practices further enhances your contribution during emergencies or disruptions. Ultimately your blend of analytical skills, interpersonal abilities, industry knowledge and unwavering commitment, makes you an invaluable asset for this role.
  
  
Degree qualification is required for this position
  
  
**For Analyst:** a minimum of three years’ experience in internal control, audit (internal or external), risk management, compliance or governance roles, preferably within a financial institution is essential for success.
  
  
Your strong attention to detail enables you to critically review information, identify gaps promptly, and deliver accurate outputs consistently.
  
  
The ability to manage multiple priorities under strict timelines demonstrates your organisational skills and commitment to dependable follow-through.
  
  
Excellent written and verbal communication skills allow you to work confidently with management as well as stakeholders across departments and locations.
  
  
Professionalism, integrity, and discretion are vital when handling confidential or sensitive information within the organisation.
  
  
A proactive approach combined with collaborative teamwork ensures you adapt comfortably in fast-paced environments while supporting colleagues effectively.
  
  
Strong proficiency in Microsoft 365 tools, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, and Copilot, to support effective record-keeping, collaboration, and communication.
  
  
Experience supporting business continuity management activities adds value by enhancing operational resilience within the division. Familiarity with incident monitoring/reporting processes strengthens your ability to respond quickly during critical situations.
  
  
**What sets this company apart:**  
MUFG stands out as one of the world’s largest financial groups committed to delivering excellence through responsible banking practices. The company fosters an inclusive workplace where every team member’s voice is valued, encouraging collaboration across departments regardless of hierarchy or location. MUFG’s dedication to integrity permeates every aspect of its operations; employees are trusted partners who contribute meaningfully toward shared goals without compromising ethical standards. By joining MUFG’s Singapore office within GCIB’s Internal Control & Administration team you become part of a global network united by mutual respect, a place where knowledge-sharing thrives alongside innovation in governance practices.
  
  
We regret to inform that only shortlisted applicants will be notified.

title: Chief Compliance Officer
description:
**The role**

We are looking for a Chief Compliance Officer to own our global compliance strategy and lead the function as we scale across markets and add licences. You will be the most senior compliance executive in the company, accountable to the CEO and the Board for an effective, risk-based compliance programme covering financial crime (AML/CFT/CPF, sanctions, fraud), regulatory compliance, licensing, and card-scheme and partner-bank obligations.

This is a builder's role. Our competitors range from large licensed neobanks with dedicated group and entity CCOs, to fast-growing crypto-payment fintechs running networks of local MLROs, to heritage card issuers launching stablecoin cards. We want someone who brings the rigour of the first and the speed of the second: a compliance leader who can earn regulators' and partners' trust while enabling the business to launch products quickly and safely.

**Key responsibilities:**

1. Strategy, governance and leadership

* Set and own the group compliance strategy, risk appetite statements and multi-year roadmap, aligned with business and expansion plans.

* Report regularly to the Board and its committees on compliance risk, key risk indicators (KRIs), material breaches, regulatory relationships and programme effectiveness; escalate material issues directly and independently.

* Build, lead and mentor a high-performing global compliance team across financial crime, regulatory compliance, licensing, operations and assurance; scale it in line with growth.

* Define a clear three-lines-of-defence model and compliance governance (policies, committees, delegated authorities) across all group entities.

* Foster a strong compliance culture through tone from the top, training and practical business partnering.

2. Financial crime (AML/CFT, sanctions, fraud)

* Own the group AML/CFT/CPF and sanctions framework; oversee the Group MLRO and local MLROs/Compliance Officers in each licensed entity.

* Oversee enterprise-wide and entity-level ML/TF risk assessments covering products, customers, geographies, channels and delivery mechanisms.

* Ensure robust KYC/KYB, CDD/EDD, PEP and adverse-media screening, ongoing monitoring and offboarding controls.

* Oversee sanctions screening (OFAC, UN, EU, UK HMT and local lists) for customers, counterparties, merchants and wallets.

* Ensure FATF Travel Rule compliance for any digital-asset or stablecoin transfers.

* Partner with Fraud and Risk on fraud typologies, scams, mule activity, chargebacks and card-to-crypto risks.

3. Know Your Transaction (KYT)

* Own one group-wide transaction monitoring and KYT framework covering fiat, card and on-chain (stablecoin/crypto) flows, so no payment rail is left uncovered.

* Oversee the transaction monitoring systems (TMS) for fiat and card activity: design detection scenarios for key typologies such as structuring, rapid movement of funds, money mules, card testing, cash-out patterns and unusual cross-border flows.

* Run a regular tuning and testing programme (threshold reviews, below-the-line testing, model validation) to keep false positives low without missing real risk.

* Set alert and case management standards: triage SLAs, escalation paths, investigation quality checks and backlog control.

* Make sure suspicious activity is reported to the right authority on time (SAR/STR/SMR), along with threshold and cash transaction reports where required.

* Run real-time and post-event KYT screening on every inbound and outbound on-chain transaction.

* Set KYT risk rules, scoring thresholds and risk appetite for wallet and counterparty exposure — e.g., sanctioned addresses, mixers/tumblers, darknet markets, scams, ransomware, high-risk exchanges and cross-chain bridge hopping.

* Select, implement and govern KYT and blockchain-analytics vendors (e.g., Chainalysis KYT, Elliptic, TRM Labs, Merkle Science), including model validation, tuning and coverage of the chains and tokens we support.

* Define what happens when KYT flags a transaction: hold, reject, freeze, return funds, request source-of-funds evidence, file a SAR/STR or exit the customer, with clear SLAs and documented decisions.

* Link KYT with KYC/KYB, fraud, sanctions and Travel Rule data so the team sees one risk picture per customer and per wallet.

* Make sure KYT controls meet the expectations of regulators, card schemes, sponsor banks and auditors, and that every decision leaves an evidence trail.

* Report transaction monitoring and KYT metrics to the Board: alert volumes, true-positive rates, SAR/STR filings, exposure trends, funds frozen or returned, and SLA performance.

4. Regulatory compliance and licensing

* Lead licence applications, renewals and variations across target markets.

* Act as, or appoint and supervise, the regulator-approved Compliance Officer/MLRO in each entity; meet fit-and-proper requirements where the CCO role itself is a controlled function.

* Serve as the primary point of contact for regulators; lead examinations, inspections, information requests and remediation programmes.

* Run horizon scanning and translate new rules (AML, payments, consumer protection, data privacy, stablecoin/virtual-asset regimes) into clear, actionable requirements.

* Ensure accurate, timely regulatory reporting and record-keeping in every jurisdiction.

5. Card schemes, partner banks and processing partners

* Own compliance with Visa, Mastercard and other scheme rules, including scheme due diligence for crypto/stablecoin-funded card programmes.

* Manage compliance relationships with sponsor/partner banks, BIN sponsors, issuers, acquirers and payment processors; meet their "flow-down" AML/KYC requirements and respond to RFIs and audits.

* Oversee merchant and programme-manager due diligence, prohibited/restricted business lists and MCC controls.

* Work with Security on PCI DSS and with Legal on data-privacy obligations relevant to cardholder and customer data.

6. Product, technology and business partnership

* Review new products, markets, partners and features from a compliance perspective before launch; embed controls by design.

* Work closely with Product and Engineering to translate regulatory obligations into scalable, automated workflows (onboarding, risk scoring, monitoring, case management).

* Own the compliance tech stack strategy (e.g., Sumsub, Sardine, Elliptic, Chainalysis, sanctions engines, case management) and drive data-led oversight.

* Advise the CEO and executive team on the regulatory implications of strategic decisions, partnerships and M&A.

7. Monitoring, assurance and reporting

* Run a risk-based compliance monitoring and testing plan; track issues and remediation to closure.

* Coordinate with Internal Audit and external auditors; support independent AML audits.

* Maintain the group policy framework and ensure policies and procedures stay current.

* Deliver role-based compliance training across the organisation, including the Board and senior management.

**What you'll bring**

**Must have**

* 12+ years of compliance and financial crime experience in payments, e-money, banking, card issuing/acquiring, fintech or virtual assets, with at least 5 years leading a compliance function.

* Prior experience as a Chief Compliance Officer, Head of Compliance, Group MLRO or regulator-approved compliance controlled function (or equivalent) in a licensed financial institution.

* Deep, hands-on knowledge of AML/CFT, sanctions, KYC/KYB, transaction monitoring and suspicious-transaction reporting across multiple jurisdictions.

* Hands-on transaction monitoring and KYT experience: building or overseeing monitoring across fiat, card and crypto/stablecoin flows, including scenario design, tuning, alert and case management, SAR/STR filing, and freeze/return decisions, using TMS and KYT tools (e.g., Chainalysis KYT, Elliptic, TRM Labs).

* Track record of securing and maintaining licences and leading regulator examinations.

* Working knowledge of card-scheme rules and partner-bank/sponsor relationships.

* Experience reporting to and challenging a Board and executive committee.

* Clean regulatory and criminal record; able to pass fit-and-proper assessments in our licensed jurisdictions.

* Excellent written and spoken English; ability to explain complex regulatory matters simply.

**Nice to have**

* Experience with virtual assets, stablecoins or crypto-funded card programmes, including Travel Rule and blockchain analytics.

* Experience in one or more of the US, EU/UK, UAE, LATAM, Canada or Comoros, plus APAC.

* Experience in a high-growth, multi-entity environment, including building compliance from scratch in new markets.

* Professional certification such as CAMS, ICA Diploma/Advanced Certificate, CFE, CCEP-I or CRCM; law, finance or related degree.

Pay: $10,000.00 - $16,000.00 per month

Work Location: In person

Transaction monitoring andalert review

Review, triage and disposition all TM alerts to defined SLAs. Document clear, auditable rationales and escalate suspicious activity to the Compliance Manager for STR consideration.

Own alert-handling procedures, QA sampling, SLAs and
  
  
performance metrics, and provide regular reports to the Head of Compliance.
  
  
**Rule and threshold tuning:**  
Analyse alert volumes, false-positive rates and typologies. Recommend scenario and threshold changes to improve coverage and reduce noise.
  
  
Blockchain investigations
  
  
**Deep-dive investigations:**  
Trace fund flows across chains and protocols, including mixers, bridges, DeFi, privacy-enhancing tools and cross-chain swaps. Identify exposure to sanctioned, illicit, darknet, scam,ransomware and high-risk counterparties.
  
  
**Typology analysis:**  
Identify emerging typologies and red flags, and turn them into monitoring scenarios and staff guidance.
  
  
**Reporting:**  
Produce clear investigation reports and case files that stand up to internal review and regulatory scrutiny. Support STR drafting and responses to law enforcement and regulatory requests.
  
  
**Tooling:**  
Make expert use of blockchain analytics platforms (e.g. TRM Labs, Chainalysis, Elliptic) and public explorers, and advise on vendor performance and coverage.
  
  
Model validation and governance
  
  
**Model validation:**  
Independently validate TM scenarios, risk-scoring and analytics models, including data integrity,coverage, threshold calibration, back-testing and below-the-line testing.Document findings and track remediation.
  
  
**Data and controls:**  
Partner with Engineering and Data teams on data quality, lineage and alert-generation logic. Support periodic reviews of the TM programme.
  
  
Policies, procedures and regulatory
  
  
**Policies and procedures:**  
Draft and maintain TM, blockchain investigation and escalation policies, SOPs and playbooks aligned with MAS requirements (Payment Services Act, MAS Notice PS-N02 and related guidelines)and BitGo global standards.
  
  
**Regulatory engagement:**  
Support MAS inspections,audits and thematic reviews, and track regulatory developments relevant to TM, the Travel Rule and digital asset AML/CFT.

5–7 years' experience in transaction monitoring, AML/CFT orfinancial crime investigations at a bank, payment institution, crypto orfintech firm, or an advisory/analytics firm.
  
  
Proven hands-on experience with blockchain analytics tools (TRMLabs, Chainalysis and/or Elliptic) and on-chain tracing across multiple chains.
  
  
Solid understanding of digital asset typologies, including mixers,bridges, DeFi, stablecoins, sanctions evasion, scams and ransomware.
  
  
Experience writing or validating TM scenarios, models orrisk-scoring methodologies, with a good grasp of testing, tuning anddocumentation standards.
  
  
Working knowledge of Singapore AML/CFT requirements for DPTservice providers (Payment Services Act, MAS PS-N02, MAS guidelines).
  
  
Strong written communication, with the ability to explain complexfindings to non-specialists and regulators.
  
  
Independent, organised and comfortable owning outcomes in a leanteam and a fast-moving environment.

Experience in a MAS-licensed entity or a regulated custodian,exchange or payments firm.
  
  
Experience with casemanagement or TM platforms, and with automation or AI-assisted review.
  
  
Experience supporting regulatory examinations or independentaudits of a TM programme.

title: Head, Community Engagement & Partnerships
description:
The Head, Community Engagement & Partnerships is a key member of AMP’s management team, contributing significantly to AMP’s leadership by shaping organisational priorities, strengthening cross-functional collaboration and shared accountability, and fostering a cohesive and inclusive management culture across AMP and its entities.
  
  
The Head provides strategic leadership and oversight of AMP's programmes and service delivery, ensuring that initiatives are responsive to the needs of clients and aligned with the organisation's mission, strategic priorities, governance requirements, and service standards. The role oversees the planning, development, implementation, and evaluation of programmes to achieve meaningful and sustainable outcomes for the community.
  
  
The Head is responsible for ensuring programme quality, managing operational risks and resources, overseeing budget utilisation, and driving continuous improvement in service delivery. The role also leads workforce and volunteer planning, develops the capabilities of staff and volunteers, and fosters strategic partnerships with government agencies, community partners, and other stakeholders to strengthen programme effectiveness and community impact. Through a client-centric and strategic approach, the Head supports organisational excellence while advancing AMP's outreach and service objectives.
  
  
MAIN DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES
  
  
1. Build Professional Partnerships and Collaborations
  
  
a) Develop and maintain strategic partnerships with other agencies, other organisations, and stakeholders to strengthen service delivery and create integrated support pathways for clients
  
  
b) Collaborate with external agencies and partners to co-design, implement, and enhance programmes that address emerging community needs and achieve desired social outcomes.
  
  
c) Develop and implement community outreach strategies to engage target client groups, strengthen community awareness, and expand the reach and impact of AMP's services.
  
  
d) Identify service gaps, emerging social trends, and community needs to inform programme development and improve the effectiveness of social service interventions.
  
  
e) Manage stakeholder engagement, communications, and feedback to foster strong relationships, gather insights, and drive continuous improvement in programmes and services.
  
  
f) Represent AMP in external engagements, sector discussions, and collaborative initiatives to promote AMP's interests, contribute to sector development, and strengthen partnerships across the social service ecosystem.
  
  
2. Planning, Theory of Change (ToC) and Programme Development
  
  
a) Develop and review the division's strategic direction, ToC, programme framework, and implementation plans to ensure alignment with AMP's mission, strategic priorities, and community needs.
  
  
b) Translate strategic objectives and desired outcomes into clear programme priorities, service models, and operational initiatives that deliver measurable outcomes for clients.
  
  
c) Identify emerging social trends, community needs, and service gaps to inform programme development, resource allocation, and service enhancement.
  
  
d) Establish priorities for programme implementation and service delivery, taking into consideration organisational capacity, stakeholder needs, available resources, and opportunities for impact.
  
  
e) Drive monitoring and evaluation of programme effectiveness and initiatives against intended outcomes and ToC, and drive continuous improvement to enhance service quality, operational efficiency, and client outcomes.
  
  
f) Work closely with internal and external stakeholders to align strategies, strengthen service integration and ToC and advance AMP's long-term social impact objectives.
  
  
g) Provide recommendations to Senior Management and the Board on programme development, sector trends, and policy changes.
  
  
h) Steward divisional performance and service delivery to achieve strategic objectives and advance AMP's mission and vision.
  
  
3. Demonstrate Corporate Governance
  
  
a) Establish and oversee programme governance, quality assurance, risk management, and compliance frameworks to ensure effective oversight, regulatory compliance, and alignment with organisational and funding requirements.
  
  
b) Drive and strengthen the division's audit, controls, and assurance framework to uphold accountability, mitigate operational risks, and ensureadherence to organisational policies, regulatory standards, and governancerequirements.
  
  
4. Manage Resources
  
  
a) Lead strategic resource planning and allocation across programmes and functions to optimise organisational effectiveness and address evolving operational priorities.
  
  
b) Establish and oversee volunteer management frameworks, policies, and practices to strengthen volunteer engagement, governance, and programme delivery capabilities.
  
  
c) Drive infrastructure, systems, and resource planning initiatives to support the division's current operational requirements and future growthneeds.
  
  
d) Oversee resource utilisation and capacity planning to ensure sustainable service delivery and optimal deployment of organisational resources.
  
  
e) Review and approve funding proposals, business cases, and resource investments to ensure alignment with strategic priorities, operational needs, and desired organisational outcomes.
  
  
5. Develop Organisational Capability for Service Delivery
  
  
a) Drive capability development strategies to strengthen the division's professional competencies, leadership bench strength, and service delivery capabilities.
  
  
b) Assess current and future workforce capability requirements and establish capability-building priorities to support the division's strategic objectives and evolving service needs.
  
  
c) Lead the development and implementation of learning, talent, and succession plans to ensure organisational readiness and sustainability.
  
  
d) Cultivate a high-performance and continuous learning culture that promotes professional excellence, innovation, and service effectiveness.
  
  
e) Strengthen leadership and management capabilities across the division to enhance organisational resilience, employee engagement, and operational performance.
  
  
f) Champion workforce planning and talent development initiatives to ensure the division is equipped with the skills and expertise required to meet current and future service demands.
  
  
SECONDARY DUTIES
  
  
a) Participate in inter-divisional project committees and render support to other department events as and when required.
  
  
REQUIREMENTS
  
  
Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership experience in the social service or related sector.
  
  
Bachelor's degree in a relevant field; postgraduate qualifications are an advantage.
  
  
Proven track record in leading programme portfolios, service delivery, stakeholder engagement, and organisational initiatives.
  
  
Experience in developing, implementing, and evaluating programmes that deliver measurable outcomes and community impact.
  
  
Experience working with government agencies, community partners, funders, volunteers, and other key stakeholders.

description:
**About Guestbook Rewards, Inc.**

**Our Guiding Principles**

**Purpose:** Help people make the most of life's opportunities to travel

**Mission:** We provide travelers the most rewarding ways to figure out where to stay, what to do, and how to make travel happen

**Vision:** A world where travelers search less and experience more

**Our Core Values**

**Focus on possibilities:** We have a positive mindset and embrace innovation

**Make an impact:** We are passionate about delivering meaningful and sustainable outcomes

**Be Accountable:** We are trustworthy and reliable to travelers, partners, ourselves, and each other

**Deliver as a team:** We embrace diversity of thought and selfless collaboration to unleash new potential

**Invest in each other:** We share knowledge and encourage continuous learning to grow together

**Job description:**

The Guestbook is the world's largest and fastest-growing loyalty program for independent and boutique brand hotels. To grow our hotel partner network across Asia-Pacific (APAC), we are in search of a Regional Development Manager who will be the consistent face of The Guestbook for hotels across APAC, from first conversation to long-term partnership.

This role will focus on developing and growing hotel partnerships across APAC, from first conversation to long-term success. You will engage hotel leads supplied by our lead generation team through outreach campaigns, book demos, and hand qualified opportunities to our Partnerships Team. As hotels join the program, you will onboard and train them, run regular performance reviews, and help them grow their direct booking revenue.

This is a fully remote position open to candidates based in Southeast Asia, such as Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, or the Philippines. Candidates must have the right to work in their country of residence and be able to travel within APAC for business. This role reports directly to the Senior Vice President of Partner & Member Experience.

**What you'll do:**

* Build a strong APAC pipeline by running multi-touch outreach campaigns to hotel leads, using email, phone, LinkedIn, and campaign-specific messaging
* Follow up consistently with leads provided by our Lead Generation Team to build interest in the program
* Tailor outreach to local markets, languages, and hotel segments across APAC
* Qualify hotels on fit, needs, and decision-making process
* Schedule demos and prepare the Partnerships Team with clear context on each opportunity
* Deliver introductory product overviews and early-stage demos where appropriate
* Hand off qualified opportunities to the Partnerships Team smoothly, with complete notes in our CRM
* Track campaign performance, including response, meeting, and conversion rates, and continuously improve messaging and targeting
* Serve as the primary contact for onboarding new APAC hotel partners, training platform end users, and providing post go-live support
* Work with our Product and Development Teams to configure the platform to each partner’s requirements and resolve technical issues
* Build credibility and partner confidence through regular communication, virtual and in-person visits, and performance reviews
* Implement direct booking strategies and share data-driven insights that help partners maximize revenue and get the most from the platform
* Increase retention of accounts, and collaborate with the Partnerships Team to support renewals and expansion opportunities
* Recommend revenue strategies and best practices as each partnership matures, drawing on deep product and industry knowledge
* Gather feedback and represent the voice of APAC hotel partners in decisions across the Product, Marketing, and Partnerships Teams
* Identify partners who can act as Guestbook advocates through testimonials, case studies, and referrals
* Travel from time to time for regional tradeshows, conferences, hotel association events, partner visits, and Team meetings

**What you'll bring:**

* 3+ years of experience in sales development, customer success, account management, business development, or another client-facing role
* Proven experience running outreach campaigns, following up on leads, and booking meetings or demos
* Experience managing a portfolio of accounts, including onboarding, training, and performance reviews
* Experience working with customers across multiple countries in APAC
* Fluent business English, plus fluency in at least one additional Asian language such as Mandarin, Bahasa Indonesia, Malay, Thai, Korean, Vietnamese, or Japanese
* Excellent written and verbal communication, with confidence presenting to hotel owners, general managers, revenue teams, and marketing teams
* Comfort with a CRM and outreach tools, and the discipline to keep records accurate and up to date
* Ability to analyze data and turn it into clear, visually appealing recommendations
